summary: Fiscal years run December 1 to November 30 and are named for the year they end
detail: FY2026 = December 1, 2025 to November 30, 2026. Worksheet columns are headed '2025-2026'; audits are 'for the year ended November 30'. period_fy is the ending year, as for the city.

summary: Year-to-date and year-end Estimate columns are not stored as facts
detail: The worksheets print 'Thru 9/30/25', 'Thru 10/6/26' or 'YTD Activity' (partial-year activity) beside the full-year columns. They are not a full-year actual or a budget, so they are not facts; they stay in data/boone_county_il/extracted/<doc>_lines.csv (measure ytd). The budget books (FY2020-FY2024) also print an 'Estimate' column (actuals through October plus an estimate for November) and, in FY2021-22, 'Actual - Aug'; neither is a full-year actual or a budget. They stay in the extracts (measure estimate, partial).

summary: Worksheet 'Total Activity' columns are preliminary actuals
detail: The 'Total Activity' column of a worksheet is the county's ledger activity for the closed year as of the document date; the audit's actual (basis actual_audited) supersedes it, and the General Fund audit schedule excludes subfunds the ledger includes.

summary: Printed worksheet totals that differ from their lines
detail: Accepted source differences, each with its reason in data/boone_county_il/overrides/<doc>.csv: FY2025 document: three funds whose printed revenue totals are 0.00 above a non-zero line (163 Sale in Error FY2025 final, 166 Schnell and 167 Wolfram memorial funds FY2024 budget and YTD); FY2027 preliminary: General Fund FY2026 revenue total $15,000 below its lines. Every other printed total equals its lines (FY2027 prints whole dollars and may differ by half a dollar per line).

summary: Prior-year budget columns of a later worksheet differ from the adopted figure on some accounts
detail: FY2025 final budget vs the FY2026 document's FY2025 budget column: 16 of 793 shared accounts differ (e.g. Public Safety Sales Tax Fund interest 8,000 vs 10,000); FY2024 budget between the FY2025 and FY2026 documents: 4 of 793; FY2026 final vs the FY2027 preliminary's FY2026 column: 8 of 790 (e.g. health insurance 2,950,000 vs 2,945,040). The document's own current column is the adopted budget (basis adopted); the later column is basis prior_doc_budget.

summary: FY2018-FY2023 audits print one 'Final Budget' column; FY2015-17 and FY2024-25 print 'Original and Final Budget'
detail: The county does not amend its budget during the year. Audits that print 'Original and Final Budget' give both bases (flag combined_column); audits that print only 'Final Budget' give basis audit_final (flag final_budget_column).

summary: The General Fund schedule is fund 001 only; the statement's General column includes subfunds
detail: From FY2020 the governmental funds statement's General column (GASB 54) adds subfunds (payroll clearing, E-Citation, forfeited funds, towing ...) to fund 001. The audit's schedule of revenues and expenditures covers fund 001 alone (FY2025: revenues 20,439,677 vs 20,566,439; expenditures 21,030,404 vs 21,073,420). FY2015-FY2019 the two agree to the dollar.
evidence: FY2025 audit combining statement - General Fund by subfund; tests/test_boone_county.py

summary: General Fund expenditure schedule totals that repeat the previous year or add a budget the lines lack
detail: FY2024 and FY2025 print a 5,000 budget on 'Total debt service' (principal and interest lines have no budget); FY2024's total expenditures variance includes it; FY2025's Total debt service actual (209,303) and Total supervisor of educational service region (84,000 / 77,995) are the FY2024 figures. Items are stored; the stale totals are not.

summary: Per-fund schedule slips in the audits
detail: FY2015 IMRF budget net change 1,657,072 (should be (19,221)); FY2016 and FY2017 Capital Projects budget net change positive (should be negative); FY2021-22 Recorder's Automation transfers out without parentheses.

summary: The audit's fund columns change
detail: FY2015-17: General, County Bridge, IMRF/Retirement, County Motor Fuel Tax, Nonmajor; FY2018-20: Other Governmental; FY2021 adds the American Rescue Plan Grant fund; FY2022-24 fold Bridge and IMRF into Other/Nonmajor; FY2025 shows Motor Fuel Tax and Bridge as major again ('Change in financial reporting entity' moves 9,398,394 out of nonmajor at December 1, 2024). Column names per audit in entities/boone_county_il/audit_fund_columns.csv.
evidence: FY2025 audit statement of revenues, expenditures and changes (page 37)

summary: Opening balances restated in FY2021 and FY2023
detail: General Fund opening balance FY2021 restated by +100,024 (Note 15); total governmental funds +850,726 (FY2020 closing to FY2021 opening) and -839,679 (FY2022 closing to FY2023 opening).

summary: Funds with no per-fund budget-and-actual schedule
detail: The per-fund schedules cover budgeted funds only; their ending balances add up exactly to total governmental funds less the General column in FY2021 and FY2022, and fall $0.2M-$6.1M short in other years (funds the county does not budget, e.g. recent bond and employee health funds). The FY2025 combining balance sheet of the nonmajor funds (60 fund columns that add to the statement's Nonmajor 20,302,376) shows which: 37 funds have a schedule and their balances equal it to the dollar; 23 do not (911 Fund 4,083,246, Probation Services 667,964, Opioid Settlement 317,934, Drug Court Grant 294,629, Law Enforcement Operations 280,162, Township Bridge 248,365 ...; 5,620,309 together), plus the 'Total' column.

summary: County employee health insurance is a General Fund transfer out to the Employee Health Care Fund in the budget books and an expense in the ERP worksheets; the audits are inconsistent
detail: The FY2020-FY2024 budget books budget it as account 899.037 'Employee Health (Care) Fund -37', a transfer out of the General Fund (2,785,000 FY2019; 2,875,000 FY2020 and FY2021; 2,620,000 FY2022; 2,570,000 FY2023 and FY2024); the ERP worksheets (FY2025 on) put 2,570,000 into 001-0000-414200 Health Ins. Employer Share as an expense and show fund 037 receiving it from 360019. The audits' General Fund budget leaves it out of expenditures (it is an other financing use) in FY2020-FY2022 and FY2024 and includes it in FY2016-FY2019 and FY2023 (differences of 2.29M, 2.76M, 2.25M, 2.84M and 2.48M against the books with the transfer excluded); the FY2025 audit includes it, spread over the functions (228,900 General control, 616,800 Judiciary, 1,721,900 Public safety = 2,567,600 = 2,570,000 less 2,400). audit_vs_budget.csv excludes the transfer from expenditure in both presentations, so the FY2019 and FY2023 differences (+2,762,000 and +2,484,000) are this line.
evidence: data/boone_county_il/audit_vs_budget.csv; FY2024_audit and FY2025_audit General Fund expenditure schedules

summary: Two FY2025 interest budgets differ between the adopted worksheet and the audit
detail: FY2025 worksheet Final Budget: Public Safety Sales Tax Fund interest 8,000 and Animal Services Donation Fund interest 800; the FY2025 audit's budget and the FY2026 worksheet's FY2025 column show 10,000 and 1,000. The county raised them after the worksheet was printed (it does not report amendments).

summary: General Fund bank charges: 2,400 in the worksheet budget, equal and opposite differences in revenue and expenditure
detail: The FY2025 audit's General Fund budget is 2,400 lower than the worksheet on both revenues and expenditures; the worksheet's Bank Charges line is 2,400. The audit appears to net the charges against revenue (not stated in the audit).

summary: Property tax collection totals that drop or repeat the Veterans Assistance collection
detail: The FY2016 and FY2017 audits print the 2013-levy collection total as 10,109,538 although the column lists the Veterans Assistance collection of 256,527 (the FY2015 audit's total, 10,366,065, includes it); the FY2017 audit lists 256,527 for the 2012 levy, a copy of the 2013 figure (the 2012 levy has no Veterans Assistance extension) and its total excludes it. The tables keep the printed lines; the later audits agree with the FY2015 audit on every other collection.

summary: FY2018 debt service to maturity: a debt certificate interest cell is 1,000 above the FY2017 audit
detail: The FY2018 audit's debt certificate interest for fiscal 2021 prints 9,658 where the FY2017 audit prints 8,658; its printed total (53,350) equals the column with 8,658.

summary: Long-term liabilities do not chain exactly from one audit to the next
detail: Ending balance equals the next audit's beginning balance on 62 of 76 line-years. The 14 others: bond premium off by 1 (FY2017, FY2019); restated opening balances (compensated absences at GASB 101 adoption, FY2024 681,225 -> 1,011,758; other postemployment benefits at the GASB 75 adoption, FY2017 -> FY2018; capital leases and notes payable regrouped in FY2021: 257,650 -> 45,588 and 197,198 -> 454,848); and the 'total' line, whose composition changes when net pension liabilities enter or leave the table (FY2016-FY2018) and when the pension liability lines are listed (FY2023-FY2024). The tables keep what each audit prints.

summary: IMRF and SLEP figures for measurement years 2014 and 2015 were restated after the FY2016 and FY2017 audits
detail: The FY2016 and FY2017 audits print the 2014 and 2015 columns of the IMRF County Regular, IMRF Elected County Officials and SLEP schedules with the values first reported (for example IMRF regular 2014 benefit payments 1,193,978, net pension liability 1,798,090); the FY2024 and FY2025 audits print 2014 and 2015 restated (1,151,674 and 1,083,983). Every measurement year from 2016 on is identical in all four audits (854 cells printed in more than one audit; 62 differ, all in 2014 and 2015). Each audit's own figures are kept; rows for 2014 and 2015 carry this exception.

summary: The fiscal year 2026 assessed valuation is the county's own estimate
detail: The 2025 tax year assessed valuation (collected in fiscal 2026) is not in any audit yet; the FY2026 budget's Projected Property Tax Rate page gives an estimate of 1,722,225,472 (its 2024 figure, 1,547,516,447, equals the audits'). It is shown flagged and replaced by the audit's figure when the FY2026 audit prints tax year 2025.

summary: Revenue by source: a few lines sit in different groups in the audits and in the budgets
detail: The comparison of General Fund revenue by source (audit_revenue_by_source.csv) is made line by line (audit_map.csv, comparable_groups.csv). All ten groups agree to the dollar in FY2024 (the first year the audit lists its lines under the budget's own headings); in FY2019-FY2023 the fees and fines, reimbursements and grants, and miscellaneous groups differ by $11,000-$137,000 because the audits and the budgets put some lines in different groups (the audit's 'Other fees' and 'Other governmental revenue' lines, jail housing fees, tax sale fees, IT services). The totals of the three groups together are closer: FY2019 +19,580, FY2020 +106,311, FY2021 +75,000, FY2022 and FY2023 -86,000 (the same General Fund revenue difference as audit_vs_budget.csv), FY2024 0, FY2025 -2,400 (bank charges). FY2015-FY2018 have no line-level budget (the FY2017 and FY2019 books print only a seven-category summary, the FY2018 book is not loaded).
